content: Our vanity is hardest to wound precisely when our pride has just been injured.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Hardship is not an unfair interruption to your real life—it is the very forge in which character is tempered. No one develops deep wisdom, empathy, or stamina by cruising down an easy path without resistance.

Across his life and work, Friedrich Nietzsche saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Like a tree that develops deeper roots when buffeted by winter gales, your past trials gave you a reservoir of strength you didn't know you possessed. You are more durable than your anxious thoughts give you credit for.
reflectionPrompt: How can you integrate the essence of this wisdom into one specific decision or encounter today?
